lessons.title: Types of specialised mowers and pre-start checks
lessons.html:
Specialised walk-behind mowers

Ordinary rotary mowers cut most garden lawns. On golf greens, bowling greens, cricket squares and fine lawns, groundsmen use specialised walk-behind mowers to get a very short, even, high-quality cut.

MowerHow it cutsUsed on
Cylinder (reel) mowerA spinning cylinder of blades cuts against a fixed bottom blade, like scissorsGolf and bowling greens, cricket pitches
Hover mowerRotary blade, floats on a cushion of airBanks and slopes
Flail mowerMany small swinging blades on a shaftLong, rough grass
Scarifier / verti-cutterVertical blades that slice into thatchRenovating fine turf

Height of cut

On a cylinder mower the height is set by moving the front roller up or down. It is measured with a setting bar or gauge. Greens may be cut at only a few millimetres; your head groundsman sets the height for each surface and season. Never take off more than about one third of the grass leaf in one cut.

Pre-start checks

  1. Read the operator's manual and only use a machine you are trained on.
  2. Check engine oil and fuel. Refuel outdoors with the engine off and cool. No smoking.
  3. Check that the cylinder and bottom blade are sharp and set correctly. A paper test: a sheet of paper should be cut cleanly across the blades (engine off, spark plug lead removed or key out).
  4. Check guards, grass box, controls, the dead-man's handle (operator presence control) and that the cylinder stops when you let go.
  5. Check tyres or rollers and look for loose bolts or leaks.

PPE

Safety boots, ear protection, long trousers, and eye protection when needed.

lessons.title: Mowing technique and maintenance
lessons.html:
Before mowing

  • Walk the area. Remove stones, sticks, golf balls, bowls and anything else. A stone can wreck a cylinder.
  • Do not mow wet greens if the head groundsman says not to; wet grass gives a poor cut and the mower can skid.
  • Remove dew by brushing or switching (with a long cane) on greens if required.

Mowing

  1. Start the engine with the drive and cylinder disengaged.
  2. Walk at a steady, even pace. Do not rush.
  3. Mow in straight lines, slightly overlapping each strip. Use a fixed point at the far end to walk straight.
  4. Turn off the green or surface (on the apron or surround) to avoid scuffing. Lift the front of the mower slightly on turns.
  5. Change direction each time you mow (for example, diagonal one day, straight the next) so the grass does not lean one way.
  6. Do a clean-up cut around the edge at the end, but not every day in the same track, to avoid wear (triplex ring).
  7. Empty the grass box before it is full so the cut stays clean. Spread or compost clippings as your supervisor says.

Safety rules

  • Never put hands or feet near the cylinder while the engine is running.
  • Stop the engine and disconnect the spark plug lead before clearing blockages or adjusting blades.
  • Never pull a mower backwards towards your feet.
  • Keep people away while mowing.
  • Never mow across steep slopes where the mower can tip.

After mowing

  • Clean grass off the mower with a brush or low-pressure water (keep water off the engine and electrics).
  • Check blades for damage. Report faults.
  • Oil and grease as the service schedule says. Record hours used.
  • Store in a locked shed.

Key points

  • Cylinder mowers give the short, fine cut needed on greens and pitches.
  • Set the height with a gauge and never remove more than one third of the leaf.
  • Clear debris before mowing and mow in straight, overlapping strips.
  • Change mowing direction each time.
  • Stop the engine and disconnect the plug before touching blades.
